about.title: Cotati Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Cotati's economy runs on a mix of small businesses, construction, retail, and light industry clustered near Old Redwood Highway and E Cotati Avenue. Workers here get hurt the same way workers do everywhere: falls, equipment failures, vehicle collisions on the job, and repetitive strain. Under California law, workers' compensation is typically your only path against your employer, no matter who was at fault. But that's not the whole story — if a subcontractor, property owner, delivery driver, or equipment manufacturer contributed to your injury, you may have a separate claim against that third party outside the workers' comp system. We handle workplace injury claims directly and can review the facts to explain what options actually exist for you. There's no obligation to move forward, and no fee unless we recover something for you.

whyChoose.title: Why You Should Talk to an Attorney First

items.title: Workers' Comp Isn't Always the Only Path
items.desc: California generally limits your claim against your employer to workers' compensation regardless of fault. But a negligent third party — a subcontractor, property owner, or equipment maker — can still be held separately liable, and we can help you sort out which applies to you.

items.title: Reporting Deadlines Matter
items.desc: You generally have 30 days to report a workplace injury to your employer, and missing that window can complicate your claim. We can help you understand what's still possible even if time has passed.

items.title: Retaliation Is Illegal, and Third-Party Claims Have Their Own Clock
items.desc: Your employer cannot legally punish you for reporting an injury. If a third party contributed to what happened, that separate claim generally carries a 2-year deadline, so getting informed early matters.

items.question: I was hurt on a job site in Cotati near Old Redwood Highway. Can I still sue someone?
items.answer: Possibly, but not your employer directly in most cases — that typically goes through workers' compensation. If a subcontractor, delivery driver, or property owner played a role in the accident, a separate claim against them may be possible. We can review the specifics of your situation for free.

items.question: What if my employer doesn't have workers' comp insurance?
items.answer: That's a serious issue and can open up other legal options beyond the standard workers' comp process. We can explain what applies given your employer's specific situation and the options available to you.

items.question: Can my employer fire me for reporting a workplace injury?
items.answer: No, retaliation for reporting a job injury is illegal in California. If you believe you've faced retaliation after an injury in Cotati, we can discuss what protections and options you may have, at no cost to you.
